cards.front: Recall a key point about Heracles and Heroes
cards.back: Heracles (Hercules in Roman) was the greatest Greek hero, son of Zeus and the mortal Alcmene

cards.front: Recall a key point about Heracles and Heroes
cards.back: Hera hated Heracles because he was proof of Zeus's infidelity — she sent two snakes to kill him in his cradle

cards.front: Recall a key point about Heracles and Heroes
cards.back: Heracles was driven mad by Hera and killed his wife Megara and their children

cards.front: Recall a key point about Heracles and Heroes
cards.back: The Twelve Labours were his punishment and path to redemption, set by King Eurystheus of Tiryns

cards.front: Recall a key point about Heracles and Heroes
cards.back: Key Labours include: Nemean Lion, Lernaean Hydra, Ceryneian Hind, Erymanthian Boar, Augean Stables, Stymphalian Birds, Cretan Bull, Mares of Diomedes, Belt of Hippolyta, Cattle of Geryon, Apples of the Hesperides, and Cerberus

cards.front: Recall a key point about Heracles and Heroes
cards.back: Heracles represents the hero who suffers greatly but achieves glory through endurance and strength

cards.front: Recall a key point about Heracles and Heroes
cards.back: Greek heroes were typically semi-divine, performed extraordinary deeds, suffered greatly, and faced death

cards.front: Recall a key point about Heracles and Heroes
cards.back: Heracles was eventually deified — after his death on a funeral pyre, he was taken to Olympus and made immortal

cards.front: Recall a key point about Heracles and Heroes
cards.back: The Labours took Heracles to the edges of the known world, symbolising civilisation overcoming chaos

cards.front: Recall a key point about Heracles and Heroes
cards.back: Other key heroes include Perseus (slew Medusa), Theseus (killed the Minotaur) and Jason (sought the Golden Fleece)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Heracles and Heroes
cards.back: Hero myths follow a pattern: divine parentage, extraordinary childhood feat, quest or challenge, suffering, and death or deification

cards.front: Recall a key point about Heracles and Heroes
cards.back: Heracles was worshipped as both a god and a hero across the Greek world
